sentence: A big branch came down in the backyard. Get rid of it and clean up the mess.

hazards.note: The fallen branch is still propped at a steep angle against the wooden fence rather than lying flat on the ground, so it could shift or drop further while being handled.

evidence.note: large branch leaning diagonally, resting its upper end against the fence and pergola-style frame, not fully grounded

hazards.note: An orange/red extension cord runs across the ground right next to the cut branch end, in the immediate work area.

evidence.note: cord visible looping across the grass and under the cut branch section

observation.model_notes: Neither photo gives a clear read on the branch's full length or whether it came from a tree still standing in this yard or an adjacent one — only the down section and one cut end are visible. Photo 2 is a close-up of just the cut end plus a hard hat and cord, so it mainly confirms the wood is already partly sectioned rather than showing overall debris extent.

counting_evidence.note: one large branch/limb (trunk-like diameter) down, spanning from the fence line diagonally across the lawn

supporting_evidence.note: close-up of the same branch's cut end, showing splintered, freshly-cut wood consistent with a large limb

evidence.note: full branch visible leaning across yard

service_lines.uncertain: Cannot tell from the photos whether this came down from a tree still standing in this yard or fell from a neighboring tree, or whether it is one large branch versus a small fallen tree top.

supporting_evidence.note: smaller cut branch pieces already lying in the grass near the main cut end

evidence.note: scattered smaller twigs, needles, and branch fragments across the lawn around and under the main fallen branch
